fields.h1: Build Clothes Survey Questions That Lead to a Decision
fields.hero_description: Build clothes survey questions on fit, color, and uniforms, with each answer stored in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Clothes Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions and the app that runs them, with branching by garment and an alert on the counts you pick.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written for your clothes

Describe the garments, the people who wear them, and the call the answers feed. Emergent writes the fit, color, and open questions, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any one.
fields.feature_2:
Skip logic by garment and size

The survey branches on earlier answers. A buyer who kept the jean answers about waist and length, and one who sent it back is asked why, with their size already filled in.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Shoppers and parents answer one question per screen on a phone. A fit rating is one tap on a 5-point scale, and a color vote shows every swatch as its own large button.
fields.feature_4:
Responses tagged by style and size

Every response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the style, the size ordered, and the order date. Filter the Arlo jean in size 32 without merging two spreadsheets.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a count crosses your line

Set a line, such as half the buyers of one style saying it runs small. The merchandiser gets a Slack or email alert once it is crossed, naming the style and the count.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, no response cap

Host the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. Responses have no cap, and on paid plans you can export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
The Arlo page now tells buyers to size up

Fernhill Denim wants to know why buyers send back its Arlo straight jean. Ten days after delivery, a fit survey goes to the 260 buyers of the Arlo. Each rates the waist, hip, and length from too small to too big. Of the 118 who answer, 64 say the waist runs small. The product page now tells buyers to size up.
fields.tab_content_2:
Of 205 votes, rust takes 88 and the fall run

Before the fall run, Tallow and Pine has to pick the color for its wool crew sweater. A vote goes to 300 newsletter subscribers, with each color shown as a photo swatch. Of the 205 who vote, 88 pick rust and 51 pick oat. Rust gets the larger order from the mill, and oat gets a short run.
fields.tab_content_3:
Polos over blazers, by 201 votes to 111

Brookvale Middle School has a uniform decision and a board vote in March. The parent council sends a survey to 450 families, and the school roster keeps it to a single answer per family. Of 312 families, 201 choose a polo with any dark pants and 111 a blazer set. The council takes the polo option to the board.
fields.tab_content_4:
96 classmates who buy secondhand, and why

For a term paper on secondhand clothes, a sociology student surveys 150 classmates. The survey asks whether they bought clothes secondhand in the past 6 months, and why. All 150 answer, and 96 say yes. Price comes first for 58 of the 96. The bar chart in the paper is drawn from the response table.

fields.hero_prompt: Build clothes survey questions for my denim brand that ask each buyer how the jean fits in the waist, hip, and length.

faq_plan.q: How do I create clothes survey questions?

plan.angle: The top 10 for clothes survey questions is lists and leftovers: Startquestion idea pages with four or five fashion questions, Pinterest pins of Instagram polls, Scribd questionnaires from student projects, a Reddit request for a uni fashion survey, and ProProfs clothing quizzes. None shows a clothes survey answering a real decision. This page covers the four jobs people mean (fit feedback after an online order, a color vote before a production run, a school uniform consultation, and a student research project on secondhand clothes), shows what each one decided, and puts question-writing advice in the how-to and FAQ.
tab_stories: Fernhill Denim emails a fit survey 10 days after delivery to 260 buyers of its Arlo straight jean; 118 answer, 64 of 118 say the waist runs small, and the product page adds a note to size up one.
Tallow and Pine asks 300 newsletter subscribers to pick 1 of 4 colors for its fall sweater; 205 answer, rust leads oat 88 to 51, and rust gets the larger production order.

Brookvale Middle School asks 450 families to choose between 2 uniform options; 312 answer, 201 choose a polo with any dark pants and 111 a blazer set, and the parent council takes the polo option to the board vote.

A sociology student surveys 150 classmates about secondhand clothes for a term paper; 96 bought something secondhand in the past 6 months, price is the top reason, and the paper's chart comes straight from the response table.
